# secopsctl gemini

AI (Gemini): generate queries, investigate alerts, summarize cases, generate playbooks

## gemini ask

Ask the SecOps Gemini assistant a question (read-only; --opt-in once per account)

```text
secopsctl gemini ask <question> [flags]
```

```text
Ask SecOps Gemini a question — YARA-L authoring help, UDM field questions,
and environment-grounded answers. Read-only: it returns an answer, it makes
no changes. The account must be opted in to Gemini once; --opt-in performs
that one-time enablement and can be combined with a question in the same run.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--opt-in` | bool | false | opt this account in to Gemini first (one-time) |

## gemini generate

MUTATING (guarded): generate a playbook draft with AI

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl gemini generate (--description <text> | --case-id N --alert <id>) [flags]
```

```text
Draft a playbook with Gemini — from a free-text description, or from a
specific alert in a case ("build a playbook for this alert pattern").
The description form is synchronous and returns the generated DRAFT
definition without persisting anything — review it and save with
`soar push playbook --file`. The by-alert form may run asynchronously —
poll it with `generate-status`. The Playbook Assistant API may reject
API-key auth by server policy; the error says so plainly.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alert` | string | - | alert id within the case |
| `--case-id` | int | 0 | SOAR case id (with --alert: draft from that alert) |
| `--description` | string | - | free-text description of the playbook to draft |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--name` | string | ai-draft | working name for the description-form draft |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## gemini generate-query

Generate a UDM query from natural language (Gemini); do not run it

```text
secopsctl gemini generate-query <natural language>
```

```text
Translate a plain-English question into a UDM query via Gemini and print it,
along with any time window the model inferred. Use `gemini search` to also run it.
```

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl gemini generate-query 'failed logins to admin accounts in the last hour'
```

## gemini investigate

AI investigation for one alert — shows existing result, or triggers a new one

```text
secopsctl gemini investigate <alert-id> [flags]
```

```text
Run (or view) the AI (Gemini) investigation for one detection alert.

Default: check for an existing completed investigation first and show it
(matching the web UI's behavior). If none exists, trigger a new one and poll
until it completes — typically a minute or two.

  --rerun   force a new investigation even if one already exists
  --latest  read-only: show the most recent investigation only (never trigger)

--json prints the full investigation record, including the embedded
investigation steps and the notebook reference.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--latest` | bool | false | read-only: show the most recent investigation (never trigger) |
| `--rerun` | bool | false | force a new investigation even if one already exists |

## gemini search

Generate a UDM query from natural language (Gemini) and run it

```text
secopsctl gemini search <natural language> [flags]
```

```text
Describe what you want in plain English; Gemini translates it to a UDM query
and runs it. If the text names a window ("…in the last hour"), Gemini's suggested
range is used unless you set --hours/--from explicitly.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fields` | string | - | comma-separated UDM field paths to project |
| `--format` | string | - | output format: table\|json\|jsonl\|csv (default: table on a terminal, jsonl when piped) |
| `--hours` | int | 24 | look-back window in hours (ignored when the model infers a window) |
| `--limit` | int | 1000 | maximum number of events to return |
| `--out` | string | - | write results to a file instead of stdout |

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl gemini search 'network connections to a public IP in the last hour'
```

## gemini summarize

Read-only: the structured AI summary of a case (reasons, next steps)

```text
secopsctl gemini summarize --id N [--refresh] [flags]
```

```text
Fetch (generating on first request) Google's AI summary of a case —
summary, reasons, and suggested next steps as structured fields. Generation
is asynchronous; the command polls until the summary settles. An existing or
in-flight summary is never re-kicked — pass --refresh to force a NEW
generation (e.g. after the case changed, or a prior generation errored).
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--id` | int | 0 | SOAR case id (required) |
| `--refresh` | bool | false | force a new generation (an existing summary is otherwise returned as-is) |
